items.title: While You Were Sleeping: 5 stories you might have missed, Oct 27, 2026 | The Straits Times
items.excerpt: Published Oct 27, 2026, 06:00 AM Updated Oct 27, 2026, 06:03 AM ## Iran holds ‘very good’ talks with Mecca pact nations on region’s security Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iran on Oct 26 in an attempt to stop the Middle East war from reigniting, with Tehran saying the discussions were “very good”. Officials from the three Mecca pact countries flew to Iran as part of efforts to “de-escalate between the parties to the current crisis”, a Saudi foreign ministry statement said. The talks, which included heavyweight Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, followed warnings by the United States, Iran and Israel that hostilities could restart in the eight-month war. ## Microsoft to offer buyouts to 60,000 workers in latest cost cut PHOTO: REUTERS Microsoft will offer buyouts to about 60,000 workers, part of the company’s efforts to trim costs and retool its workforce for the artificial intelligence era. Some personnel in the US, Canada, India and the UK at a vice-president level and below will be eligible, said a Microsoft spokesperson. Divisions such as Xbox, Windows, Copilot and finance are fully participating in the offer, according to people familiar with the terms. Certain pools of employees, including some focused on data centres, sales, marketing, cybersecurity and quantum computing, aren’t eligible, the people said. Microsoft declined to comment on these specifics. ## Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo draws early complaints of the screen cracking ... The iPhone Duo, one of Apple’s biggest new products in years, is drawing a growing number of complaints from customers who say the foldable display cracked after just hours or days of use. In these cases, customers reported hearing a crunching sound when unfolding the phone, followed by a large crack forming along the centre crease. Some users also experienced a white patch or other display malfunction on the right side of the screen. Reports of the problem first surfaced on Reddit and other social media sites. Bloomberg News has since independently verified the issue with more than half a dozen customers, who provided photos showing damage to their devices or evidence of their support conversations with Apple. ## Jordan says its air force struck ‘militant hideouts’ in Syria after church attack ... Jordan said on Oct 26 its air force struck what it described as militant hideouts in southern Syria after determining that the suspects behind last week’s deadly church attack in the kingdom were linked to “terrorist groups” operating there. The armed forces said the operation was conducted in coordination with Damascus. Syria’s government gave a contradictory account, saying it had launched an investigation into the Jordanian attacks, and stressed in a statement the importance of field and security coordination in border areas. Damascus informed Jordan of its “complete reservation” over the strikes without prior coordination, the foreign ministry said in a statement.

items.excerpt: Published on: Oct 27, 2026, 08:40:21 IST ... ## India's UNSC reforms push India has emphasised on expanding the right to "veto" to all UNSC member states. Parvathaneni Harish, India's Permanent Representative to the UN, said that the privilege of the veto carries an immense burden of responsibility that requires restraint. "Limiting the veto cannot be separated from the questions of categories of membership, regional representation, size and working methods. We need to move forward on all five clusters together. India reiterates its call for a comprehensive approach towards Security Council reforms," he said. ## Trump says Brazil election looked ‘rigged’ US President Donald Trump said on Monday, October 26, that Brazil’s presidential election looked like it was “rigged,” without citing evidence. Leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term in office in a comeback over his right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. “It looked like another rigged election, frankly,” Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland. “I didn’t take sides, but it was a terrible look for the world. Elections have to be indisputable, and it looked really bad to me.” On being asked if he would “do something about the election,” Trump responded, “I am not running Brazil, I’m running the USA.” ## Cyclone Arnab intensifies into very cyclonic storm Cyclone Arnab has intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal and is likely to move northwestwards before crossing the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, near Yanam, by the forenoon of October 28, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on October 27 and 28, Odisha on October 28, Chhattisgarh on October 28 and 29, and East Uttar Pradesh on October 29. ... ## Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or Harry Kane on Tuesday became the first English footballer since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the men’s Ballon d’Or, capping a remarkable season for the Bayern Munich and England forward. The 33-year-old beat Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe, who finished runner-up, and World Cup winner Lamine Yamal, who came third, to claim the prestigious prize. Kane, who also won the Men’s Striker of the Year award, became the first Bayern Munich player to win the Ballon d’Or since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who claimed the honour in consecutive years in 1980 and 1981.

items.excerpt: ## Counting begins for 19 Legislative Council seats in Bihar, UP Vote counting for 19 Legislative Council seats across Bihar and Uttar Pradesh began at 8 am today with tight security. The elections cover eight seats in Bihar, comprising four graduates’ and four teachers’ constituencies, and 11 seats in Uttar Pradesh, including five graduates’ and six teachers’ constituencies. In Bihar, 150 candidates are contesting the eight seats and polling on October 23 recorded an 82.85% turnout in teachers’ constituencies and 53.42% in graduates’ seats. The BJP and its ally JD(U) have fielded candidates for four seats each, while Prashant Kishor’s Jan Suraaj Party is contesting all eight. In Uttar Pradesh, counting is being held across seven cities – Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut, Jhansi, Bareilly and Gorakhpur. Authorities have made security arrangements and put CCTV surveillance and videography measures in place. The counting process may take longer as the elections follow the single transferable vote system under proportional representation.

items.excerpt: ## A ceasefire in Oleshky (Ukraine) is about to take effect. According to the TASS news agency, a partial ceasefire in the city of Oleshky (Kherson province) is expected to take effect from 4:00 AM on October 27 (Moscow time, which is 8:00 AM the same day in Vietnam), to facilitate humanitarian operations in the Russian-controlled area of ​​Ukraine. Earlier, Russia stated its willingness to consider further localized ceasefires for humanitarian purposes, but affirmed that it would not reduce the intensity of its military operation in Ukraine. Notably, just hours before the ceasefire was scheduled to take effect, Ukrainian officials accused Russia of attacking the capital Kyiv on the evening of October 26, resulting in at least one death, eight injuries, and extensive damage to buildings. According to Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko, the explosions shattered windows at two medical facilities, while one person was reported killed near a supermarket and a 20-year-old girl was injured near a university dormitory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of using ballistic missiles to attack a university campus and residential areas, asserting that there were no military facilities near these locations. Russia has not commented on the allegations.

items.title: US business activity cools in October; strong demand fueling price pressures By Reuters
items.excerpt: Published Oct 23, 2026, 09:49 AM Updated Oct 23, 2026, 09:55 AM ... By Lucia Mutikani WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US business activity slowed modestly in October, though robust demand allowed companies to raise prices for goods and services, a sign that inflation could increase further and remain persistently high in the coming months. S&P Global said on Friday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, slipped to 57.6 this month from a five-year high reading of 58.4 in September. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. Strength in manufacturing was offset by a slight pullback in the vast services sector. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid footing following what is expected to have been a strong performance in the July-September quarter. Economists expect the government’s advance gross domestic product report next week to show the economy growing at around a 3.0% annualized rate last quarter, mainly driven by consumer spending and business investment in AI. The economy has so far not shown any signs of buckling under the weight of the oil price shock stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran, with savings, generous tax returns in the spring, tariff refunds, a strong stock market performance and corporate profits providing a cushion. Economists warned that the inflation fallout from the drawn-out Middle East conflict was likely to slow consumer spending this quarter. The survey’s measure of new orders received by businesses edged up to 58.2 this month, the highest level since March 2022, from 58.1 in September. The increase was mostly in the services sector, with S&P Global noting "rising domestic demand, boosted partly by precautionary stock building" and growth in exports. Its gauge of prices for output rose to 59.8, the highest reading since August 2022, from 58.4 in September. Businesses across manufacturing and services sectors raised prices. Delivery performance by suppliers to manufacturers deteriorated further. The survey’s measure of suppliers’ delivery times dropped to a more than four-year low of 38.1 from 40.9 in September. SUPPLY BOTTLENECKS INTENSIFYING "Cost pressures remain a key concern," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "Supply chain bottlenecks have meanwhile intensified, and order book backlogs are growing, making it easier for companies to pass higher costs on to customers." Consumer and producer prices increased strongly in September, the government reported this month, raising concerns that inflation was fanning out across the economy. The Federal Reserve in September raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range. Economists expect the US central bank to stand pat at its meeting next week and hike borrowing costs again in December. The survey’s measure of prices paid by businesses for inputs slipped to a still-high 64.9 from 65.9 in September. Manufacturers, however, faced higher prices this month, with the index still near four-year highs. Though overall ... A measure of factory employment increased to the highest level since March 2012, with Williamson saying that companies were seeking "to boost capacity to fulfill stronger customer demand."

items.title: Fed survey shows price pressures intensifying amid rise in fuel costs By Reuters
items.excerpt: Published Oct 14, 2026, 02:23 PM Updated Oct 14, 2026, 02:24 PM Oct 14 (Reuters) - The US labor market remained stuck in a low-hire, low-fire state and inflation was intensifying across parts of the country in recent weeks, a Federal Reserve report showed on Wednesday, underscoring what’s at stake as the central bank weighs whether to deliver a second straight interest rate hike later this month. While businesses in much of the country have a positive outlook, their "expectations tend to be for slight growth, weighted toward manufacturing and burdened by persistent uncertainties," the Fed said in its latest "Beige Book" report, a compendium of survey-based data and commentary from businesses compiled by its 12 regional banks to provide a read on economic conditions. "Firms reported elevated diesel prices and noted that fuel surcharges were passing on increased costs throughout the supply chain," said the report. It noted that three of the Fed’s 12 districts described price growth as robust and eight as moderate, with three noting it was "intensifying." "Contacts in multiple Districts also noted continued price pressure from other commodities, tariffs, and insurance," it said. The survey also acts as something of a barometer for the economic pressures voters are dealing with ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine whether President Donald Trump’s Republican Party maintains control of Congress. The cost of living is the top issue cited by voters in a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll. The Fed increased its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range last month, and most policymakers have indicated another hike will likely be needed this year, though probably not until December. Financial markets are pricing about a 37% chance of a rate hike at the Fed’s October 27-28 meeting after data on Wednesday showed consumer prices rose 3.7% in the 12 months through September, far faster than the central bank’s 2% target and above the consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters. Higher gasoline costs from the Middle East war were largely to blame for the higher CPI reading, with fast-rising software and toy prices also pointing to the impact of AI-driven demand and higher tariffs under Trump’s trade policy.

items.title: DOJ asks Washington state to set aside 400 ballots from voters it says may be noncitizens
items.excerpt: Oct. 26, 2026, 9:08 PM EDT By Jane C. Timm The Trump administration Monday targeted another Democratic-led state in the midterms by asking Washington to sequester ballots in next week’s election that it says could be cast by noncitizens. The acting U.S. attorney in Washington, Neil Floyd, asked the Washington secretary of state to review a list of more than 400 registrants the Justice Department believes are noncitizens and sequester any ballots they cast. “We have identified over 400 non-citizens who are registered to vote and have voted in multiple elections,” Floyd said in a news release Monday. “This is only the tip of the iceberg. We will continue to investigate and identify those who are committing crimes by voting illegally.” The request came the same day the Trump administration suffered a legal setback in its push to separate thousands of ballots in California as it seeks to inject the federal government into tallying and certifying the 2026 election results. NBC News first reported last week that the Justice Department was considering bringing more requests to states with mail elections that send mail ballots to all registered voters. In a letter sent to Washington election officials that was shared with NBC News, the Justice Department gave the state 24 hours to review the list for citizenship records. Washington, which has more than 5 million voters on its voter rolls, refused to share its unredacted voter rolls with the Justice Department this year. Floyd criticized the state for that, saying Monday that it made his work more time-consuming. In an interview with conservative radio host Jason Rantz that was published Monday, Floyd said his office checked lists of permanent legal residents like green card holders against voter registration records in their search. Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs’ office is reviewing the list, spokesperson Helen Smith said in an email, though Hobbs criticized the request in a statement. “We take our responsibility to protect voter information seriously and will only respond to requests that follow due process. We saw what happened in California and don’t want Washingtonians to be harassed,” he said. “The timing of this request—one week before the General Election—is no doubt intended to cast unfounded suspicion on the results.” Noncitizens do end up on the voter rolls sometimes, though relatively few vote, since it’s a crime with a paper trail and one that can incur serious penalties, including deportation. Newly naturalized citizens are frequently flagged as noncitizens in voting records, in large part because there is no comprehensive list of U.S. citizens.

items.excerpt: By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters Published On 27 Oct 2026 27 Oct 2026 A United States appeals court has ruled against the administration of President Donald Trump in its bid to block the state of California from counting certain mail-in ballots this election cycle. In a decision on Monday, the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals denied a request from the government to sequester roughly 20,000 mailed ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm election. The Trump administration had asserted that the ballots were sent to people who are “likely” non-citizens. But it has not publicly revealed how it created its list or determined that the voters identified upon it were ineligible due to their citizenship status. In a two-to-one decision, the appeals court said the Trump administration had not given lower courts enough time to review the case. It therefore declined to stop California’s ballot tabulation. The court’s majority also underscored that election administration was the state’s responsibility under the US Constitution. The Trump administration was asking “the federal court to dictate to a state legislature a matter squarely within the state’s traditional domain”, Judge Gabriel Sanchez wrote in his opinion. Sanchez also warned that granting the Trump administration’s petition would be “inviting disorder and confusion for voters and election officials alike”. The Trump administration filed its lawsuit against California on October 15, less than three weeks before the midterm vote on November 3. California is a Democrat-led state, and Trump, a Republican leader, has repeatedly made unfounded claims that the state is prone to “cheating” in its elections. The case is currently being weighed in a lower court, with a hearing scheduled for Tuesday. But the Trump administration sought an expedited decision from the appeals court, pointing to the looming election date. The midterm elections are critical to determine which political party holds power in Congress. Currently, the Republican Party maintains slim majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate, but experts project the Democratic Party is on track to make significant gains, flipping one or both chambers. In the lead-up to the midterms, Trump has raised the prospect of non-citizen voting as a threat to election integrity. But experts say such voting is rare. California officials have likewise cast doubt on the administration’s claims of 20,000 ballots going to “likely non-citizens”, and they framed the administration’s lawsuit as an effort to interfere in the voting process. “At best, this litigation is a reckless political stunt,” lawyers for California Secretary of State Shirley Weber said in a court filing on October 20. “At worst, it threatens to disenfranchise thousands of Californians this election.” Trump’s Department of Justice has sued 30 states and Washington, DC, for complete access to voter rolls that include sensitive personal data. It has argued that releasing such information is necessary to prevent alleged voter fraud. But the department has lost 26 of those cases thus far, with opponents successfully arguing that such manoeuvres could scare away voters and interfere with state election administration. The Trump administration has yet to win any of the 30 cases. Despite claims to the contrary by Trump and his allies, cases of illegal voting, including by non-citizens, are few and far between. Non-citizens are barred from participating in federal elections in all 50 states in the US. In July, an investigation by the news service Reuters found only 129 cases of noncitizens being charged by federal authorities with illegal voting since 1996. Many of those cases involved mistakes, like administrative errors or individuals being uncertain of voting rules, rather than fraudulent intent. Voting rights advocates have also pointed to flaws in how the Trump administration has identified potential non-citizen voting, signalling some eligible voters may be disenfranchised as part of its efforts. Immigration agents under Trump have been assigned to ferret out non-citizen voters, in some cases knocking on doors to inquire about the citizenship status of the residents inside. Last week, the administration charged 28 immigrants in California with illegally voting. But reporting from the Los Angeles Times found that some of the accused reacted to the charges with confusion and maintained that they never registered to vote.

items.excerpt: # First Day First Show Tuesday | 27 October, 2026 ### Around Tinsel Town Legendary music composer Deva passes away Tamil film music composer Deva, who brought gaana music into mainstream cinema and whose songs and background scores for Rajinikanth-starrers such as Annamalai, Arunachalam, and Baashha became hugely popular, died on Saturday (October 17, 2026), aged 75. Deva’s music bridged seemingly disparate worlds — the earthy rhythms of Chennai’s gaana tradition, the mass appeal of Tamil cinema, and the melodic richness of classical and devotional music. items.excerpt: October 26, 2026 | 7:03 pm ## Benilde holds free horror film fest FOR Halloween, LAGIM! Benilde Film Horror Festival is returning with a collection of thrillers and horror films to be screened for free at the Benilde Design + Arts Campus in Manila. Organized by the Film Department of the De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde (DLS-CSB), the third iteration of the annual fete will run for two days with a total of 12 short films on view. Set A is slated for Oct. 28 while Set B is scheduled for Oct. 29. LAGIM! is free and open to the public. It will run from 5:30 to 8:30 p.m. on the scheduled dates. Each set will be followed by a talkback session with the filmmakers. It will be held at the 12 th Floor Screening Room of the Benilde Design + Arts Campus, 950 Pablo Ocampo St., Malate, Manila. Registration is available at tinyurl.com/2026Lagim and is open to students of other colleges and universities. Capacity is limited to 150 registrants per day. ... ## SHANNi releases EP with launch party YOUNG artist SHANNi has dropped a new EP titled Cure For Loneliness via Sony Music Entertainment. The five-track release finds her moving seamlessly between Manila Sound, soft rock, sunshine pop, jazz, and indie pop, bringing a more sophisticated touch to songwriting and arrangement. Across five tracks, SHANNi explores the complexities of love and human connection. She co-produced it with Max Cinco, supported by recording engineer Marcus Mababangloob of Meadowlark Productions, digital mixing engineer Jet Francisco of Wild Grass Studio, and analog mastering ... An EP launch party will take place at Theodore Events Place in Marikina City on Oct. 31, 6 p.m. ... ## Apl.de.Ap reps PHL heritage in new EP GLOBAL music icon Apl.de.Ap has returned to his roots with the release of his new EP under GMA Music entitled PPP. Standing for “Power to the Pilipino People,” the three-track EP marks a deeply personal chapter in Apl’s journey as an artist, serving as a love letter, a rallying cry, and a testament of devotion to his home country. One of its singles is “Why,” a collaboration between Apl and OPM rockstar Bamboo. Another is “Pinoy United,” featuring the King of Moro Songs, Datu Khomeini. PPP is out now on all digital music streaming platforms nationwide. ## LISA’s EP out now RAPPER, singer, and dancer LISA has released her EP PRESS PLAY via LLOUD Co./RCA Records. The six-track project is created with a movie in mind, so fans can sit down, and “press play.” Alongside the EP, she has released the music video for the focus track, “Tarantino,” which follows LISA’s action-packed journey through a hotel to deliver a note to her favorite director, Quentin Tarantino. PRESS PLAY includes the previously released single “SaWaDiKa,” referring to the Thai greeting for “hello.” Its accompanying music video was shot in the pop star’s native Bangkok, with the single itself debuting at #69 on the Billboard Hot 100, her highest so far on the chart. PRESS PLAY is out now on all digital music streaming platforms.

The album features the original songs from the show co-written by co-written by the project’s executive music producer Larrance “Rance 1500” Dopson and Jason “Problem” Martin. Also included is John’s Theme by Terrace Martin. The soundtrack will be released digitally tomorrow, October 27 by Hollywood Records. The streaming/download link will be added to this page within the next day. The label has previously released multiple EPs/singles over the last couple of weeks. The Drop: A Snowfall Saga is created by Malcolm Spellman based on the original Snowfall series and stars Gail Bean, Isaiah John, Asante Blackk, Peyton Alex Smith and Simmie Sims III. The drama follows Snowfall characters Wanda Bell & Leon Simmons as they fight to reinvent themselves in ’90s Los Angeles, where the fallout from the crack epidemic is fueling a new game: the rise of West Coast rap.
